latest_findings.claim: At d_model=256 (seed 22, m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, N=128, 6000 steps), N=128 trained force R2 at the best-margin layer is 0.79523 at layer 1 (control 0.65467, margin 0.141, headroom-normalised 0.41). That clears the >= 0.74 prediction and is 0.077 above the d128 value (0.718). However, the gap to the paired d256 N=64 arm could not be computed because run-20261016-050924-d030 is still running. accel_step R2 is 0.91127 at layer 1 (control 0.71358, margin 0.198). Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.69: inside [0.60, 0.90] but 0.18 below the d128 seed-22 value of 0.868, so the 'accel_step stays flat' condition fails.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The force part of expected_if_true happened, and by a wide margin. The deciding criterion did not get tested: the best-layer gap (<= 0.085) and the layer-1 same-layer gap (<= 0.10) both need the paired d256 N=64 arm, which has not finished. If that arm lands near the d64/d128 N=64 values (0.8235 at layer 1, 0.82669 at layer 4), the gap would be about 0.03. That would support a capacity bottleneck, but this is an estimate, not a measurement. The accel_step criterion also fails. The normalised margin fell from 0.868 to 0.69, but the trajectory's max-over-layers accel_step R2 is 0.97 while layer 1 reads 0.911, so the drop may come from higher d256 controls (0.714) or from a different best layer rather than a real loss of decodability. The d128 reference's layer would need checking. Controls rise steeply with width: distance control is 0.916 and energy control 0.912, so both fail the 0.1 bar even though trained R2 is 0.97-0.99. The force control (0.655) is also above the d64 values, which is why the hypothesis compares on trained R2. This is a single seed and a single arm. val_mse_ratio is not monotone (0.28 at step 1500, 0.57 at step 2000), but it ends at 0.0127. The verdict becomes supported if the paired arm gives a best-layer gap <= 0.085 and the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact. It becomes refuted only if the paired N=64 arm comes in at >= 0.895, which is implausible given its d64 and d128 values.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 on data_seed 1 (m2 fixed at 0.5, 6000 steps), N=64 force beats its control in both seeds and stays well above the paired N=128 arm. Seed 22: R2 0.86504 vs control 0.6763 (margin 0.189). Seed 23: R2 0.88223 vs control 0.69995 (margin 0.182). Both are at layer 1. Against the N=128 layer-1 values (0.79972 and 0.83083, from f-20261016-043058-4504), the same-layer gaps are +0.065 for seed 22 and +0.051 for seed 23. Those gaps are smaller than the d_model=64 data_seed 1 gaps (about 0.086 and 0.053). At N=64, accel_step (layer 1) is decoded much better than force: R2 0.935 and 0.929 vs controls 0.752 and 0.759, giving headroom-normalised margins of 0.738 and 0.704. But the pre-registered rule that accel_step matches across arms holds only in seed 23 (difference 0.029). In seed 22 the difference is 0.084 against the N=128 value of 0.654.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The force part of expected_if_true was met in both seeds. Both N=64 force margins are at least 0.1, and both N=64 minus N=128 gaps are at least 0.04 at the best-margin layer. Both arms peak at layer 1, so the best-layer gap and the same-layer gap are the same comparison, with no cross-layer pairing. The verdict is inconclusive, not supported, because one pre-registered condition failed: in seed 22 the headroom-normalised accel_step margin differs between arms by 0.084, more than the 0.05 allowed. That difference is also in the opposite direction to a pure force-specific deficit, because N=64 also decodes accel_step better at layer 1. So part of the N=128 shortfall at layer 1 may be a general layer-1 decodability gap, not something specific to force. I could not open the N=128 run files directly. The N=128 values (0.79972, 0.83083, 0.654, 0.675) are taken from f-20261016-043058-4504 and the related open question, not read from those runs' probes_final here. Both runs completed 6000 of 6000 steps. Seed 23's gap (0.051) is close to the 0.04 bar, and there are only two seeds. Things that would change this verdict: (1) N=128 layer-1 values read from the files that differ from the quoted ones; (2) comparing at matched val_mse_ratio, which differs here (N=64 0.0051/0.0029); (3) a third seed, which would show whether the accel_step mismatch in seed 22 is noise. If the accel_step condition is dropped as a secondary control, both seeds support the claim that the force deficit is not a width bottleneck on data_seed 1.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 on data_seed 1 (m2 fixed at 0.5, N=128, 6000 steps), force beats its control at layer 1 in both seeds. Seed 22 has R2 0.79972 vs control 0.67491 (margin 0.125) and seed 23 has 0.83083 vs 0.69211 (margin 0.139). These are below the paired N=64 d128 arm, whose layer-1 force margins are 0.189 and 0.182 in its trajectory. That gives estimated N=64 minus N=128 force gaps of about 0.06-0.07 for seed 22 and about 0.04-0.05 for seed 23. Both are same-layer (layer 1) comparisons, but they are approximate, because the paired arm's unrounded probes_final values are not available here. accel_step is decoded better than force and its gain over control is larger relative to the room left above that control: R2 0.9052 vs control 0.72617 (seed 22) and 0.91185 vs 0.729 (seed 23), giving headroom-normalised margins of 0.654 and 0.675, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.88]. The N=64 normalised accel_step margin could not be computed, so the 'within 0.05 of N=64' part is untested.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The evidence leans toward the deficit persisting at twice the width on data_seed 1, but the pre-registered test cannot be fully scored. (1) The pre-registration requires paired N=64 values from probes_final, unrounded. Those values are not in this context. The N=64 numbers above come from rounded trajectory margins (0.189/0.182 at layer 1) and the max-over-layers R2 field (0.867/0.882). Taken as max R2 minus N=128 probes_final R2, the gaps are 0.067 (seed 22) and 0.051 (seed 23). Taken as the difference in margins, they are 0.064 and 0.043. In this experiment, the max-over-layers force field overstates the layer-1 R2 by 0.002-0.011, so seed 23's gap could be as small as about 0.04, which is on the bar. (2) The accel_step 'within 0.05 of N=64' criterion is untestable. In the N=128 runs, accel_step's max-over-layers R2 (0.971-0.975) is far above its best-margin layer-1 R2 (0.905-0.912), so per-layer controls for N=64 cannot be inferred from the trajectory. Compared with the d_model=64 data_seed 1 gaps (about 0.086 and 0.053), width seems to shrink seed 22's gap by roughly 20% and seed 23's by very little. This is broadly consistent with the 25-40% shrink seen on data_seed 0 (f-20261016-012922-fd3b), but it is a one-dataset, two-seed comparison. If the N=64 probes_final at layer 1 put both gaps at 0.045 or more and the N=64 normalised accel_step margin within 0.05 of 0.65-0.68, the verdict becomes supported. If seed 23's gap is below 0.04, it stays inconclusive (split). If both gaps are 0.02 or less, it is refuted. Both runs completed all 6000 steps.

latest_findings.claim: At e<=0.9, the 3000-step layer-4 accel_step R2 settles well below the matched e<=0.85 values in all 3 seeds. Seed 70: 0.457 vs 0.573, gap 0.116. Seed 71: 0.421 vs 0.558, gap 0.137. Seed 72: 0.447 vs 0.588, gap 0.141. accel_step still beats its control (margins 0.305/0.271/0.277, controls 0.15-0.17), and the headroom-normalised margin is 0.360/0.319/0.334, all below 0.40. R2 rose only 0.011-0.064 from the 600-step values (0.393/0.396/0.436) and was flat within about 0.01 from step 1000-2250 onward, while val_mse_ratio kept falling about 10x (about 0.12 to 0.013-0.015). Force also beats its control but is much weaker and less stable than accel_step. Force R2 is 0.310/0.200/0.373, with margins 0.140/0.131/0.212 and normalised margins 0.17/0.14/0.25. Its best layer is 4/1/2 depending on seed, while accel_step peaks at layer 4 in every seed.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed the full 3000 steps (none stopped early). All gaps clear the 0.08 bar by at least 0.036, and the margins and normalised margins pass with room to spare, so the verdict does not depend on borderline numbers. Limits: (1) The e<=0.85 reference values come from a different experiment (f-20261013-001616-659c). The comparison assumes the same data_seed, pipeline version and best-of-5 control draw, and if the reference R2 had been read at a different layer or under an older control scheme the gaps could shift by a few hundredths. (2) Only one data_seed and one architecture (d_model=64, 4 layers) were tested, so the 'lower ceiling' is a ceiling for this model and a linear probe. A nonlinear or log(accel_step) probe, or a wider model, could still decode much more. (3) Seed 71 was still gaining about 0.005 per 250 steps at the end, so a longer run might narrow its gap somewhat, though not by the 0.10 needed to reach the 'false' band. The verdict would change if a 6000+ step run brought any seed within 0.04 of its e<=0.85 value, or if matched-layer, same-pipeline e<=0.85 reruns turned out much closer to these values.

latest_findings.claim: At matched 24000-step horizon (m2 = 0.5, data_seed 0, seed 22), N=64 final layer-1 force R2 = 0.80399 (control 0.57407, margin 0.230, best layer 1). That is 0.114 above the same-layer N=128 value of 0.6903 (run-20261015-214139-70d4) and 0.099 above N=128's best layer (layer 3, 0.70462; cross-layer comparison). accel_step R2 = 0.95241 at layer 4 (control 0.72946, headroom-normalised margin 0.82). The pre-registered horizon check failed: layer-1 force at step 12000 of this run is about 0.794-0.796 (control plus margin), which is 0.044 below the 12000-step run's endpoint of 0.8398 (run-20261014-043150-f21c), above the 0.03 tolerance. This run's 24000-step endpoint (0.804) is also 0.036 below that 12000-step endpoint.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Every gap criterion passes by a wide margin. Same-layer gap 0.114 and cross-layer gap 0.099, against the 0.04 bar and the 0.02 refutation line. Force margin 0.230 >= 0.1. accel_step normalised margin 0.82 is inside [0.60, 0.85]. The run completed all 24000 steps. The verdict is inconclusive for one reason: the pre-registered horizon check failed by 0.044, and the hypothesis said that outcome must be reported as horizon-confounded. That failure does not weaken the matched-horizon N=64 vs N=128 comparison, since both runs are 24000 steps. It does show that seed-22 N=64 force depends on the lr schedule. Force peaks at about 0.806 at step 6000, dips to about 0.795 at step 11000, and recovers only to 0.812 (trajectory max) by step 24000, even though val_mse_ratio falls about 8x to 0.00095. Comparisons between the 12000-step and 24000-step runs are therefore not like-for-like. A matched-loss reading points the same way. At steps 12000-13000 (val_mse_ratio 0.008-0.004), N=64 layer-1 force is about 0.796, roughly 0.09 or more above N=128's 0.69-0.70 at a similar loss. Limits: this is one seed on one dataset, intermediate values come from 3-decimal trajectory fields, and the step-12000 value assumes the step-12000 control equals the final layer-1 control (0.57407, the same as the reference run's control). Two things would change the verdict to supported: rerunning the horizon check against a schedule-fraction-matched checkpoint (step 6000 of the 12000-step run versus step 12000 here), or a second seed showing a same-layer gap >= 0.04 at 24000 steps on data_seed 0. A same-layer gap below 0.04 in such a replication would weaken the ceiling interpretation.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261016-042740-1339 (issue 0): Accepted. The pre-registration required citing both reference runs. run-20261015-214139-70d4 (N=128 seed 22, 24000 steps, layer-1 force R2 0.6903, best layer 3 at 0.70462) and run-20261014-043150-f21c (N=64 seed 22, 12000 steps, layer-1 0.8398) should be in evidence_run_ids alongside run-20261016-022408-42ac. I repeated an omission I had already accepted on f-20261016-022923-3654. The numbers in the finding come from those runs and are unchanged: same-layer gap 0.114, cross-layer gap 0.099, horizon check failed by 0.044. Status stays inconclusive.

Response to review r-20261016-042740-1339 (issue 1): Accepted. The pre-registered horizon check compares step 12000 here (about 0.795) with the 12000-step run's layer-1 endpoint (0.8398). That check failed, and the result stays horizon-confounded. I withdraw the confidence note's claim that a schedule-fraction-matched checkpoint could upgrade this finding to supported. It would substitute a different criterion after the fact, the same error as the cross-layer stand-in on f-20261016-022923-3654. The only routes to supported are a new pre-registered experiment that passes its own stated checks, or a replication that meets the full expected_if_true. Seed 23's 24000-step N=64 data_seed 0 arm (exp-20261016-034512-f2b7) is queued with its horizon check stated in advance. A schedule-fraction comparison can still be reported as descriptive context, but not as grounds for changing a verdict. Status stays inconclusive.

config.hypothesis: This is the reference arm of the width-scaling test. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=256, best-of-3 controls, seed 22, 6000 steps. Prediction: N=64 force is saturated in width. Final trained force R2 at the best-margin layer (probes_final, unrounded, layer reported) stays within 0.03 of the same seed's d_model=128 N=64 value of 0.82669 (layer 4, run-20261016-002356-cbfe) and of the d_model=64 value of 0.8235 (layer 1, run-20261014-031344-3f3d). If so, any change in the N=64 minus N=128 gap with width comes from the N=128 side. Layer-1 force R2 is also reported. The headline gap against the paired d_model=256 N=128 arm uses best-margin layers, and cross-layer pairs are flagged. A layer-1 same-layer gap is reported wherever both arms list layer 1 in probes_final. Both arms' run IDs are cited. If the paired arm is unavailable, the gap is reported as not computed. Width comparisons use trained R2, not margin, because random controls rise with d_model. No band is placed on control R2.
